problem: VLMs for Embodied Question Answering excel at perception and semantics but ignore physical constraints such as reachability, producing unrealistic or overconfident answers; existing methods only encode constraints in visual features and leave reachability to be learned implicitly.
motivation: Physically grounded EQA needs feasibility reasoning (can the robot actually reach or act on something), especially in multi-robot settings. Implicit learning of reachability yields false positives in reachability judgment, so explicit symbolic constraints are needed to guide the model.
key_idea: Turn reachability and semantic cues into soft symbolic predicates composed with differentiable fuzzy logic, and inject the resulting constraints into both multimodal fusion and prompt-based decoding.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract claims that explicit fuzzy-logic constraints, applied at both fusion and decoding stages, reduce reachability false positives and improve action feasibility reasoning compared with implicit learning.
method: Soft symbolic predicates: reachability and semantic cues are converted into continuous-valued predicates.
Differentiable fuzzy logic: predicates are composed via continuous logical operators into symbolic constraints.
Constraint injection into multimodal fusion: the constraints guide how visual and language features are fused.
Constraint injection into prompt-based decoding: the constraints steer answer generation toward physically feasible answers.
